subject: Amortized uplift & dynamic billing buckets for mid-cycle expansion
messages:
From: Hannah Schultz <hannah@omnixhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@omnixhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-cycle top-up — request to amortize across Q3/Q4

Hi Diego,

We’re accelerating a pilot and expect roughly a 35% uptick in generate usage over the next two quarters. Legal/Finance here at OmniX asked whether Redwood can provide billing options other than a single up-front invoice for the full top-up.

Ideally we’d like:
- An option to amortize the additional committed spend across the remaining months of our current term (Q3 + Q4).
- Clear invoice line items so our AP team can code spend to different GLs if needed.

Can you send a few concrete options (pro-rata immediate invoice, amortized monthly schedule, and an annualize+co-term option with discount tiers)? Also include any required contract amendment path so we can circulate internally.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schultz
Director of Data & ML, OmniX Health
[hannah@omnixhealth.com]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schultz <hannah@omnixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle top-up — request to amortize across Q3/Q4

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear ask. Appreciate the heads up on usage. Below are three pragmatic options we can move forward with; I attached a simple workbook that lays the math out for a $120k uplift example (uplift_amortization_v1.xlsx).

Option 1 — Pro-rata immediate invoice (no amortization):
- One invoice for the exact added commit from the date of amendment to the term end.
- No discount applied.
- Fastest to provision; good if you need capacity immediately and want simple accounting.

Option 2 — Amortized billing (recommended for AP smoothing):
- Spread the uplift evenly across the remaining billing cycles (monthly or quarterly).
- Standard uplift discount: 5% off the uplift when amortized across the remaining term.
- Invoice will show: (a) base renewal line (unchanged), (b) uplift amortization line (monthly charge), (c) usage true-up line at renewal.

Option 3 — Annualize + co-term at renewal (best unit-economics):
- Convert the uplift into an annualized additional commit and co-term at your next renewal date.
- Discount: up to 10% on the uplift portion if converted to an annual commit at signing.
- Requires an amendment; we’ll issue a new SOW and can route via DocuSign.

Additional notes and operational points:
- Split/invoice line items: we can emit multiple lines and custom memo fields for GL coding.
- Usage carryover: current policy is no carryforward of unused commit, but we can include a 60-day grace credit for minor shortfalls (documented in amendment).
- Amortization math and examples are in the attached workbook.
- If Finance needs split invoices (e.g., 40/30/30 across three months), we can implement that on a one-off basis — we just need the exact schedule and PO.

Next steps: tell me which option you prefer and your legal contact. If you want Option 3, I’ll draft the amendment and route for signatures. If Option 2, confirm term end date and desired monthly vs. quarterly amortization.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernández
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189
[Attachment: uplift_amortization_v1.xlsx]

From: Hannah Schultz <hannah@omnixhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@omnixhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle top-up — request to amortize across Q3/Q4

Diego — thanks, this is really helpful. A couple clarifying Qs from Finance/Procurement before we pick: 

1) If we choose amortized billing (Option 2), what does the invoice look like month-to-month? Can it show the original subscription line + a separate amortized uplift line?
2) Is the 5% amortization discount applied only to the uplift portion or to the total invoice?
3) For Option 3, will the 10% discount require the uplift to be paid up-front or can we still invoice annualized commit monthly?

Quick follow-up: our PO team needs to see GL code fields and the proposed invoice dates (we prefer charges to align to end-of-month). Also looping in Laura (finance) to help with PO/GL.

Thanks — Hannah

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle top-up — request to amortize across Q3/Q4

Hannah/Laura — answers inline below.

1) Invoice layout for Option 2 (amortized):
- Invoice will include: (A) existing subscription line (pre-amendment amount), (B) "Amortized Uplift - month X" line showing the uplift slice, (C) memo field that contains the amendment id and PO number.
- We can set the invoice date to the last business day of the month and issue a single PDF that lists each month’s amortized line.

2) Discount application:
- The 5% amortization discount applies only to the uplift portion; your base subscription pricing remains unchanged.

3) Option 3 payment cadence:
- If you choose to annualize and co-term, you can still elect monthly invoicing for cashflow reasons, but the full annualized commit must be contractually committed up-front. The 10% discount is contingent on that annual commitment (i.e., contractually agreed annual number).

Operational / timing proposal:
- If Finance wants split invoices (example: 40%/30%/30% over three months), we can set three invoice lines with those amounts and distinct invoice dates. Provide the PO# and GL codes and we’ll populate the amendment.
- As an incentive to close quickly: if OmniX signs the amendment within 7 business days, we can increase the amortization discount to 7% (applies to uplift only).
- I attached a draft amendment (amendment_draft_v1.pdf) that shows the wording we’d need for Option 2 and Option 3.

Please advise which path you want and copy in the legal contact for the SOW route. Happy to jump on a 20-min call to walk the spreadsheet with Laura — Marissa and Ben are on standby for implementation questions.

Best,
Diego
[Attachment: amendment_draft_v1.pdf]

— Hannah
